ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, each small square in the grid has a side length of \(1\), and the vertices of \(\triangle ABC\) are all located at grid points. What is the sine value of \(\angle ABC\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
$\because AC=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=2\sqrt{5}$, $AB=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=2\sqrt{5}$, \\
$\therefore AC=AB$, \\
$\because CD=BD=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore AD\perp BC$, \\
In $\triangle ABD$ with a right angle, \\
$AD=\sqrt{AB^2−BD^2}=3\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore \sin\angle ABC=\sin\angle ABD=\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{5}}=\boxed{\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}}$.

method.method_draft: From the figure, read the directions of the two rays forming angle ABC. From B to A, the path moves 4 units left and 2 units down, so relative to the leftward horizontal its acute inclination has tangent 2/4=1/2.
